questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code fans events out to connected sockets and cleans up connections? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A user has tabs open on two different server nodes and an event is published once through publishSessionEvent. How many copies of the message does each of the user's sockets receive?
choices: Two, because both the publishing node and the subscription deliver it
None on the second node, because socketsByUser is per-process
One per node, but only the first socket on each node
One, because every node delivers only from the subscription callback to its own local sockets

questions.prompt: A client on a poor mobile connection stops reading, and 400 KB of events accumulate in its socket's send queue. What happens at the next event for that user?
choices: The event is queued as well, since ws.send buffers without limit
sendToUser terminates that socket and skips it, while other sockets of the user still get the event
All of the user's sockets are closed with code 4001
The event is dropped for that socket only, and the socket stays connected

questions.prompt: A user's sockets close one by one while the hub is iterating over that user's sockets in sendToUser. Why does the code spread the Set into an array before looping?
choices: So that the loop works on a stable snapshot while close handlers and terminate() calls remove sockets from the live Set
Because a Set cannot be iterated with for...of
Because it makes sends to different sockets run in parallel
To avoid sending the same message to a socket twice
